Set in the ancient realm of Sicily, the narrative revolves around two unemployed potters who embark on a daring venture—co-directing a theatrical production performed by Athenian prisoners of war. The New York Times heralded the book as "a comic riff on Greek tragedy, with an Irish accent," while Roddy Doyle praised it as "a tale of modern-day Dubliners living among ancient Greeks." Currently residing in Norwich, Lennon reflects on the origins of "Glorious Exploits." His fascination with ancient Greece dates back to his childhood. A pivotal moment came when he delved into "History of the Peloponnesian War" by Thucydides, a detailed account of the 27-year conflict between Athens and Sparta. Intrigued by Athens' decision to launch an unprovoked invasion of Sicily, primarily targeting Syracuse, Lennon found inspiration for his novel. Thousands of Athenian prisoners were subsequently executed by being thrown into a quarry outside Syracuse, a grim outcome that Lennon sought to explore through his storytelling."
